# Northfield Cook-Line Doneness Check Log
Dinner service, 06/18/2026 | Grill station | Shift lead: Megan Brennan

## Check standards
| Item | Required endpoint | Recorded check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Beef steak, medium-rare | 130–135°F | 132°F, probe check |
| Ground beef patty | 160°F | Not recorded |
| Chicken breast | 165°F | 166°F, probe check |

## Shift notes
- Caleb Petrov checked the steak at 6:42 PM after resting it for 3 minutes. The cut was intact, the center was warm red, and the juices were clear.
- Reject the steak as below the 130°F minimum; return it to the grill for further cooking.
- Brandon Fitzgerald checked the chicken breast at 6:51 PM with a calibrated, sanitized probe inserted into the thickest part. The reading was 166°F; serve after the scheduled rest.
- For ground beef patties, use color and clear juices as the doneness check before plating.
- Megan Brennan washed hands between raw and ready-to-eat handling, and sanitized the probe between checks. Record the food, time, and actual probe reading on the station sheet before the plate leaves the pass.

## Service handoff
The steak and chicken checks were completed during the first dinner push. Keep the probe at the grill station, clean and ready for the next batch; do not rely on appearance alone when a thermometer check is specified. Any item below its listed endpoint must be returned to heat and checked again before service.

errors.quote: Reject the steak as below the 130°F minimum
errors.explanation: The table records the steak at 132°F, within its stated 130–135°F endpoint. The instruction to reject it as below 130°F contradicts that recorded check.
errors.fix: Accept the steak as within the 130–135°F endpoint

errors.quote: For ground beef patties, use color and clear juices as the doneness check before plating.
errors.explanation: The line omits a thermometer check against the listed 160°F endpoint. Color and clear juices cannot establish that ground beef has reached a safe internal temperature.
errors.fix: For ground beef patties, verify at least 160°F with a probe thermometer before plating.
